Situation "Self-doubt & inner criticism" for subtype SO7. Autopilot: Self-doubt is embedded in a higher meaning: Maybe this pain is part of the way. Maybe I'm growing. The reframing strategy protects you from really feeling the doubt. Awareness: What if this doubt is just doubt - without a higher meaning, without a framework for growth? What would you do then? Exercise: Sit with doubt for ten minutes today – without transforming it. Name it: “I’m doubting right now that…” Then breathe. That's enough.

Situation "Loss & grief" for subtype SO7. Autopilot: Loss is clothed in meaning: perhaps that was its meaning. Maybe you'll grow from it. The search for meaning helps - but sometimes too early, before the pain was really there. Awareness: What if this loss still doesn't make sense - and that's okay right now? Can grief be meaningless before it becomes meaningful? Exercise: Today, write down what you have lost – no meaning, no morals, no growth. Only: That was, and now it is no longer. How does that feel?

Situation "Overwhelm & pressure" for subtype SO7. Autopilot: You envision yourself from the pressure: Everything will soon get better, the big picture makes sense. The energy flows into ideas and plans - while the concrete excessive demands remain. Awareness: What specifically needs to be done today – beyond all visions? What one thing is really moving you forward today? Exercise: Today, write a list of a maximum of three tasks. Only three. Do them before planning new ones. Watch how satisfying that is.

Situation "Stagnation & inner emptiness" for subtype SO7. Autopilot: You bridge the void with visions and plans: the next big project, the next adventure, the next meaning. The stagnation remains invisible behind the ideas. Awareness: What if you didn't create a new vision today - but sat with the now? What is really there right now? Exercise: Spend an evening without planning today. No notebook, no brainstorming. But: what happens now? Let the answer emerge quietly.

Situation "Exhaustion & burnout" for subtype SX7. Autopilot: Without high-intensity stimulation, ordinary life feels incredibly flat and stale. You frantically search for the next emotional high, the next magnetic encounter, or the next inner fire. The void of quiet emptiness feels almost impossible for you to tolerate. Awareness: What if the quiet right now is actually a much-needed breathing room, rather than the opposite of being alive? What would you hear if you just held still? Exercise: Dedicate yourself to a single, simple activity today—like cooking, walking, or sketching—and practice being 100% present in it. No multi-tasking, no switching. Observe if something quiet opens up inside you.

Situation "Conflict & dispute" for subtype SX7. Autopilot: In conflict, the energy can suddenly become very high - passionate, convinced, almost enthusiastic about your own position. And then, just as suddenly, your interest wanes and your mind is somewhere else. Awareness: Do you really take the other person's conflict seriously - even if your interest in it is already waning? Exercise: Stay with the topic until the end - even if it has stopped being exciting. Question: “Have we really sorted this out?”

Situation "Loneliness & withdrawal" for subtype SX7. Autopilot: Loneliness is overwritten with the next adventure, the next intense experience or the next passionate connection. As long as there are sparks, you feel alive and connected. Awareness: What if you stuck with a single connection today - and deepened it instead of changing? What could happen there? Exercise: Choose a relationship that is important to you and consciously invest in it today - a conversation, a moment of real presence. No distractions, no next topic.

Situation "Decision making stress" for subtype SX7. Autopilot: The decision is based on the intensive connection: What holds us together? What strengthens what connects us? Your own needs and long-term perspectives can be lost sight of. Awareness: Are you currently deciding for the connection – or for yourself in the connection? Is there a difference and do you know it? Exercise: Ask yourself: What would I choose if this connection wasn't at stake? Take this answer as one of the votes in your decision.

Situation "Relationship crisis" for subtype SX7. Autopilot: The crisis of the relationship becomes all-or-nothing: either everything is right – or it ends. One demands complete clarity, complete commitment, complete presence. Nuances will not be tolerated. Awareness: What if this relationship is neither perfect nor over - but simply in a difficult moment? Is there a space in between that you haven't considered yet? Exercise: Ask the other person, without immediately judging: “What do you need from me – specifically, today?” Then respond with what you can give. Not what would be ideal – what is really possible.

Situation "Self-doubt & inner criticism" for subtype SX7. Autopilot: Self-doubt is overwritten with the next excitement: a new idea, a new project, a new connection. Intensity protects against the silence in which doubt would have to be heard. Awareness: What would you hear if you paused the excitement for a moment and really listened – to yourself? Exercise: Pause today before jumping to the next idea. Ask yourself in silence: What am I doubting right now – really? Let the answer come without solving it immediately.

Situation "Loss & grief" for subtype SX7. Autopilot: Loss creates intense reactions: pain that quickly turns into new intensity - a new experience, a new person, a new idea. The energy moves on before the grief can settle. Awareness: What if you stayed with what you lost today - without moving on? What shows up when you hold still? Exercise: Take a moment today to remember what was lost. No distractions, no moving on. Only: I was here, that was real. I miss it.

Situation "Overwhelm & pressure" for subtype SX7. Autopilot: Overwhelm is combated with intensity: you dive deeper into what brings you joy, jump to new experiences, and look for the next energy. The pressure stays in the background until it breaks. Awareness: What if today you channeled the energy you put into new experiences into the task you have left behind? Exercise: Today, choose a task that you keep putting off. Kill them in one go - then treat yourself to something nice as a real reward afterwards.

Situation "Stagnation & inner emptiness" for subtype SX7. Autopilot: Without intensity, life feels stale: you look for the next exhilaration, the next encounter, the next fire. The emptiness is almost unbearable. Awareness: What if silence is a breathing space and not the opposite of life? What would you hear if you held still? Exercise: Today, stick to a single, simple activity—cooking, walking, drawing—and be fully involved. No changing. Watch to see if anything opens.

Situation "Exhaustion & burnout" for subtype SE8. Autopilot: Stagnation is utterly intolerable to your system: you fight violently against it, manufacture artificial pressure, and immediately hunt for the next target. A standstill feels like a defeat. You direct all your energy against the emptiness—and completely exhaust yourself in the process. Awareness: What if you chose not to fight the stagnation today—and instead just allowed the standstill to be there? What would that mean for you? Exercise: Give yourself permission to move absolutely nothing forward today. Spend half a day with zero agenda, zero pressure, and zero fighting. Observe what organically emerges in the quiet when you lay your weapons down.

Situation "Conflict & dispute" for subtype SE8. Autopilot: In conflict, power is used – clear, direct, sometimes overwhelming. You want to force clarity, organize the field, end the matter. Others may feel overwhelmed. Awareness: Are you currently fighting for the issue – or for control? What if you didn't have to win the conflict? Exercise: Take a step back in the conflict - literally or figuratively. Give the other person space to speak without interrupting. Watch what happens.

Situation "Loneliness & withdrawal" for subtype SE8. Autopilot: Loneliness is not easily admitted – it feels like weakness. You stay active, independent, strong. But underneath sometimes lies a deep longing for someone to whom you can really show yourself. Awareness: Is there anyone you could really show yourself to – without performing at your strength? And do you allow that? Exercise: Today, seek closeness to someone you trust - not to do or create something. Just to be there. Together. Observe what this triggers in you.

Situation "Decision making stress" for subtype SE8. Autopilot: Decisions are made quickly and clearly - hesitation is seen as weakness. You act before all the information is there because waiting feels wrong. Sometimes a bad decision is better defended than reversed. Awareness: What if you paused this decision for a moment - not out of fear, but out of strength? Who makes the better choice: the one who acts immediately or the one who really looks first? Exercise: Wait 24 hours before implementing this decision. The next day, ask yourself: Is this still my choice? If yes – then act with full force.

Situation "Relationship crisis" for subtype SE8. Autopilot: You fight or you cut out. Either the conflict is addressed directly and harshly - or you retreat behind strength, show nothing and carry on. Both leave little room for real connection. Awareness: What if you took one step towards the other in this crisis - without weakness, but without armour? What would happen between you then? Exercise: Say something real to the other person today - not the demand, not the strength. Something that shows you're really there: "I really care about this relationship."

Situation "Self-doubt & inner criticism" for subtype SE8. Autopilot: Self-doubt exists – but is not shown. Outwardly: strength, control, determination. Inside: sometimes a deep question as to whether you are really as strong as you seem. This question is fought instead of answered. Awareness: What if you didn't fight the doubt, but let it stand for once? Strength does not eliminate doubt - it still exists. Exercise: Today, write a sentence that begins with "I'm unsure if..." - just for you, not an audience. Then read it. This is you too.

Situation "Loss & grief" for subtype SE8. Autopilot: Loss triggers resistance: you fight, repress, and overcome the pain with strength. Grief feels like weakness - so it is fought. That takes strength without healing. Awareness: What if grief isn't a weakness - but a sign that something really mattered to you? Can that be strong? Exercise: Today, allow yourself to be sad – not angry, not strong, just sad. Ten minutes, in silence. You don't have to show this to anyone. Only allow yourself.

Situation "Overwhelm & pressure" for subtype SE8. Autopilot: Overwhelm manifests itself as a compression: more energy, more control, more pressure on others and yourself. You fight through instead of prioritizing. The body will get in touch at some point. Awareness: What if you stopped putting pressure on yourself today and instead left things out? What is really not urgent? Exercise: Today, cross three things off the list that you wanted to do today. Don’t postpone – really let go. Then observe: Has something broken?

Situation "Stagnation & inner emptiness" for subtype SE8. Autopilot: Stagnation is not tolerated: you fight against it, create pressure, look for the next goal. Standing still feels like weakness. The energy is directed against the emptiness - and becomes exhausted. Awareness: What if you didn't fight the stagnation today - but just let it be there? What would that mean? Exercise: Allow yourself not to move today. Half a day with no agenda, no pressure, no fighting. Observe what arises in the silence when you don't fight.

Situation "Exhaustion & burnout" for subtype SO8. Autopilot: Without an active battle to fight or a group assignment to protect, your inner engine completely stalls. You frantically search for a new adversary, a fresh challenge, or a massive project—anything to bridge the uncomfortable silence of the void. Awareness: What if real power today doesn't look like fighting—but rather looks like pausing, getting quiet, and deeply listening? What would that stillness tell you? Exercise: Sit down with someone from your group today—not to direct them, lead them, or fix their problems, but simply to listen: How are things going with you guys? What do you really need right now?

Situation "Conflict & dispute" for subtype SO8. Autopilot: In a conflict that concerns someone who belongs to one's own group, the reaction can be very quick and very large. Protection goes beyond proportionality. The energy is there immediately. Awareness: Is what's happening really a threat - or is your protective impulse reacting to something it reads as a threat without really examining it? Exercise: Before you intervene: First ask the affected person what they need. Maybe she needs something other than protection.

Situation "Loneliness & withdrawal" for subtype SO8. Autopilot: Loneliness shows itself as a need for protection for others - you surround yourself with your own group, care for them, keep them together. Your own aloneness is dissolved in the service of others. Awareness: Who cares for you – not as a leader, not as a protector, but as a human being? Is there anyone you allow to do this? Exercise: Today, allow yourself to be cared for by someone - even if it feels unusual. Accept care without immediately reciprocating it.

Situation "Decision making stress" for subtype SO8. Autopilot: You decide for the group - what holds it together, what protects it, what strengthens the common position? One's own preference is subordinated to the collective benefit, sometimes without realizing it. Awareness: Are you currently deciding for the group – and would you choose the same if it was just you? Do you know the difference? Exercise: Talk through the decision with yourself first: What do I want? Then: What does the group need? Then decide which voice should really lead here.

Situation "Relationship crisis" for subtype SO8. Autopilot: You protect your own people - and anyone who becomes a threat in this circle is confronted or excluded. Relationship crises within the protective circle are sometimes overlooked because people look outside. Awareness: Is there someone in your inner circle that you weren't really listening to right now - because you were busy protecting instead of connecting? Exercise: Sit with this person today – without protective impulses, without leadership gestures. Just ask, “How are you and us?” Then listen.

Situation "Self-doubt & inner criticism" for subtype SO8. Autopilot: Self-doubt is declared a threat: it is fought, pushed away, and overwhelmed by even more commitment to the group. Anyone who doubts themselves protects others even more - as if that would erase the doubt. Awareness: What if instead of fighting the doubt, you showed it to the person you really trust – and talked to them about it? Exercise: Today, tell someone you really trust what you doubt. Not packaged as a weakness - as a fact: "I'm currently unsure whether..." Let the answer come.

Situation "Loss & grief" for subtype SO8. Autopilot: You share the group's grief while holding back your own. Strength for others – that is the role. Your own pain goes unseen because it endangers your strength. Awareness: Who carries your pain - when you are carrying everyone else? Is there someone you can show your sadness to today? Exercise: Today, find someone you really trust and say, "I'm grieving right now." Just that. No explanation, no strength. Let him answer.

Situation "Overwhelm & pressure" for subtype SO8. Autopilot: You take responsibility for the group beyond your own boundaries: those who lead do not give in. Your own state of exhaustion is ignored or hidden from others. Awareness: What if, as a leader, you set boundaries today - and thereby set an example instead of showing weakness? Exercise: Today, delegate a specific task that you would normally take on yourself. Be clear about what you need. Let the other person do it – without controlling.

Situation "Stagnation & inner emptiness" for subtype SO8. Autopilot: Without fighting or protecting the group, there is no drive. You look for a new enemy, a new challenge, a new project - to bridge the void. Awareness: What if strength today lies not in fighting - but in pausing and listening? What would the silence tell you? Exercise: Sit down with someone in the group today – not to guide or protect, but to hear: How are you? What do you need?

Situation "Exhaustion & burnout" for subtype SX8. Autopilot: Without an intense focus or an adversary to push against, ordinary life feels completely flat and meaningless. You restlessly hunt for the next spark, the next conflict, or the next massive challenge—just to feel alive. Awareness: What if vitality is just as possible in total stillness—without a battle to fight or a fire to light? What actually remains of you when everything goes completely quiet? Exercise: Go out into nature alone today—with no destination and no task to complete. Sit down somewhere and let the quiet wash over you. Ask yourself: *Who am I when I am not fighting?*

Situation "Conflict & dispute" for subtype SX8. Autopilot: In conflict there is no holding back - the full energy is there immediately, direct, intense, demanding. Not a step back. That can clarify – and it can destroy. Awareness: Do you take a moment before you jump in full force - just to check if this is the right situation for that energy? Exercise: Take a breath before you answer—not to hold back, but to choose. What do you say when you choose instead of react?

Situation "Loneliness & withdrawal" for subtype SX8. Autopilot: Loneliness triggers a deep hunger for merger - for a connection that encompasses and fills everything. When this connection is missing, a nagging inner lack arises. Awareness: What do you really need at this moment – ​​fusion, or just real contact? Is there a person for whom simply being there would be enough? Exercise: Today, seek simple physical closeness – a conversation, a shared silence, a walk next to each other. Not intensity, but presence.

Situation "Decision making stress" for subtype SX8. Autopilot: Decisions are made impulsively and with full force - or focused on the most important person: What suits us, this connection? Your own quiet voice is lost in the intensity. Awareness: What do you – yourself, calm and clear – want in this decision? Is there an answer within you that you haven't really heard yet? Exercise: Go for a short walk alone. Ask yourself: What would I choose if no one knew about it? Then write down the answer.

Situation "Relationship crisis" for subtype SX8. Autopilot: The crisis is overwhelmed with intensity - people fight hard, demand complete clarification, fusion, commitment. If the other person cannot maintain this, there will be a total withdrawal. Awareness: Is what you're asking for right now really what the relationship needs - or is it what you've always been looking for inside? Is there a difference? Exercise: Give the other person a specific wish today: “I wish that…” – and fill it with something achievable. Not the ideal. The possible.

Situation "Self-doubt & inner criticism" for subtype SX8. Autopilot: Self-doubt comes as a shock - and is immediately answered with intensity: more energy, more determination, more strength. But the actual doubt remains untouched underneath. Awareness: What would you hear if you let go of the intensity for a moment - and just be there with the doubt without fighting it? Exercise: Today, go into absolute silence – no conversation, no music, no cell phone – for twenty minutes. Let whatever comes come. Then name it in a sentence.

Situation "Loss & grief" for subtype SX8. Autopilot: Loss creates intense energy: anger, pain, sadness - everything comes at once and with full force. This can be overwhelming. The intensity sometimes protects us from really feeling the vulnerability. Awareness: What lies beneath the anger or intensity? What is the quiet core of this loss – beyond the force? Exercise: Walk in silence today – no conversation, no music. Ask yourself: What am I really missing? Let the answer come quietly. It doesn't have to be loud.

Situation "Overwhelm & pressure" for subtype SX8. Autopilot: Overwhelm is met with intensity: you push through, fight, don't give in. The line between healthy biting and self-damaging pressure is blurring. Awareness: Where is the line between powerful and self-damaging? What advice would a mentor you trust give you today? Exercise: Today, pause before you make a decision under pressure. Three breaths. Then decide. Watch to see if the decision changes.

Situation "Stagnation & inner emptiness" for subtype SX8. Autopilot: Without intensity and opponents, life feels flat. You look for the next fire, the next conflict, the next challenge - just to be alive. Awareness: What if aliveness is also possible in silence – without fight, without fire? What remains of you when everything is quiet? Exercise: Go out into nature alone today – without a goal, without a task. Sit somewhere and let the silence come. Ask yourself: What am I if I don't fight?

Situation "Exhaustion & burnout" for subtype SE9. Autopilot: Stagnation feels familiar and almost comfortable to your system: you keep moving in the same old groove, avoid making hard decisions, and endlessly procrastinate. The inner emptiness is sedated by routine rather than broken through. Awareness: What if you made just one tiny, crystal-clear decision today—not a massive life change, just a small choice? What would that shift for you? Exercise: Select one specific item that you have been putting off for a long time. Take the very first step toward tackling it—just the first step. Commit to doing it for five minutes. Then stop and see what happens.

Situation "Conflict & dispute" for subtype SE9. Autopilot: In conflict lies the impulse to avoid it, to mitigate it, to invoke it. You give in, agree, make yourself smaller - to keep the peace. Something accumulates inside and eventually breaks out. Awareness: What are you swallowing right now – and how long will it last? Exercise: Express your clear, calm opinion in this conflict - not to fight, but because you have an opinion. Watch what happens when you show up.

Situation "Loneliness & withdrawal" for subtype SE9. Autopilot: Loneliness is filled with habits: watching TV, eating, scrolling, dozing. You numb being alone without really feeling it. The withdrawal becomes invisible because it is so familiar. Awareness: What are you numbing right now – and what would emerge if you really felt it? Exercise: Create a habit today: Before you pick up your phone or turn on the TV, pause for a moment. What do you really need? And is what you're about to do really that?

Situation "Decision making stress" for subtype SE9. Autopilot: You don't really decide - you let it be decided. The situation, the habit, the coincidence take over. One follows the path of least resistance without consciously choosing. Awareness: Did you make this decision – or did it just happen? What would it be like to really choose for once, even if it costs discomfort? Exercise: Set yourself a clear decision moment: Today, at [time], I make this choice. Capture this moment. Write down what you chose and why.

Situation "Relationship crisis" for subtype SE9. Autopilot: One hopes that the crisis will resolve itself. You wait, evade, do something else - and the tension between those involved grows because it is never really addressed. Awareness: Is it really dissolving at the moment - or are you repressing it and hoping it will lessen? What would happen if you initiated the conversation today? Exercise: Say to the other person today, "I want to talk to you about something that's bothering me." Just this sentence. Then see what comes.

Situation "Self-doubt & inner criticism" for subtype SE9. Autopilot: Self-doubt is numbed: I'm okay, it'll go away. You resort to habits, withdraw, carry on - and the inner voice that wants to say something falls silent in everyday life. Awareness: What would you hear if you put the habits aside for a moment and really ask: How am I actually feeling - honestly? Exercise: Today, write down what your inner critic says - and then write next to it what a benevolent friend would say. Let both voices stand next to each other.

Situation "Loss & grief" for subtype SE9. Autopilot: Loss becomes embedded in routine: you carry on, anesthetize yourself with everyday life, postpone the pain. The loss is somewhere, but it doesn't get space because space feels dangerous. Awareness: What are you carrying with you that hasn't had a place yet? What if you set aside just ten minutes for your pain today? Exercise: Sit today with a photo or a reminder of what was lost. Ten minutes. Let whatever comes come – even tears, also emptiness, also silence. Everything is allowed.

Situation "Overwhelm & pressure" for subtype SE9. Autopilot: Overwhelm is carried quietly: you carry on, don't say anything, hope that things get better on their own. The pressure accumulates until it results in exhaustion or sudden withdrawal. Awareness: What are you wearing right now that you shouldn't be wearing alone? Is there anyone you could tell today what's too much? Exercise: Write down today: What is too much? Which of these can you give away? Tell a person specifically what you need - even if it feels strange.

Situation "Stagnation & inner emptiness" for subtype SE9. Autopilot: Stagnation is familiar and almost comfortable: you keep going in a rut, avoid making decisions, procrastinate. The emptiness is numbed by routine rather than broken. Awareness: What if you made a small, clear decision today - not the big one, just a small one? What would that change? Exercise: Today, choose something that you have been putting off for a long time. Take the first step – just the first. Five minutes. Then see what happens.

Situation "Exhaustion & burnout" for subtype SO9. Autopilot: You live entirely for the harmony of the group, and you lose your personal drive in the process: *Where am I going? What do I want?* These questions are permanently sidelined because the group provides your sense of direction. Awareness: What do you want—you yourself, entirely for you, without worrying about the group? Is there a personal desire that has been waiting on the shelf for a long time? Exercise: Write it down plainly today: *If I were allowed to decide completely on my own, without disappointing a single soul—what would I do next?* Then consider if you can brave the very first step.

Situation "Conflict & dispute" for subtype SO9. Autopilot: In a conflict, you take on the perspectives of everyone involved and try to mediate, connect and smooth things over. Your own position often disappears. In the end, you no longer know exactly where you stand. Awareness: What is your own opinion in this conflict - not the balanced synthesis, but really yours? Exercise: Just formulate your own point of view without taking the other person's position into account. Just: “I think…” and then a clear sentence.

Situation "Loneliness & withdrawal" for subtype SO9. Autopilot: Loneliness is hardly recognized as such - you merge with your surroundings, your mood, your everyday life. Being alone runs in the background while you deal with the outside. It only appears in quiet moments. Awareness: When was the last time you really sought contact for yourself - not because it happened, not because someone else wanted it, but because you wanted it? Exercise: Initiate an encounter yourself today – don’t wait for someone to come. Choose active. Observe what it feels like when you approach someone out of yourself.

Situation "Decision making stress" for subtype SO9. Autopilot: You adapt: ​​What does the group expect? What would be acceptable for everyone? Your own voice is pushed back so far that you can hardly hear it anymore. Awareness: What would you choose if you decided only for yourself - not as part of the group, not as someone who keeps harmony? Is there that voice within you? Exercise: Write down what you want - without considering others. Not to implement it immediately, but to know it. This voice has a right to be heard.

Situation "Relationship crisis" for subtype SO9. Autopilot: You adapt, mediate, take on all perspectives - and in the process you lose your own. The crisis is resolved through mediation rather than through clarification. Nobody knows what you actually want. Awareness: What do you want in this relationship – really you, not as a compromise, not as a synthesis? Does this answer exist within you? Exercise: Tell the other person clearly what is important to you about this relationship - not as a demand, but as your own truth: "It's important to me that..." Let him answer.

Situation "Self-doubt & inner criticism" for subtype SO9. Autopilot: Self-doubt leads you to adapt even more: if I just do enough of what others need, the doubt will diminish. But it grows because your own voice becomes quieter and quieter. Awareness: Whose expectations is your inner critic currently trying to fulfill – and are they really your own standards? Exercise: Ask yourself today: What would I do if I were as caring toward myself as I am toward others? Then do just one thing.

Situation "Loss & grief" for subtype SO9. Autopilot: You grieve silently in the group, adapting your pain to the collective. Your own loss merges with the shared one - and your personal depth remains untouched. Awareness: What do you personally lose – not the group, not the community, but you? Is there a pain of its own underneath? Exercise: Today, write down what this loss means specifically to you – not to others, not to the group. Just your perspective. Just your pain.

Situation "Overwhelm & pressure" for subtype SO9. Autopilot: You harmonize under pressure: nod, take over, give in - to keep the peace. Your own excessive demands remain invisible because conflicts are avoided. Awareness: What did you agree to today that was actually too much? And what would have been a friendly, clear no? Exercise: Today, in a situation where it becomes too much, say calmly and kindly: "I can't take on that right now." Just this sentence. No buts, no excuses.

Situation "Stagnation & inner emptiness" for subtype SO9. Autopilot: You live for the harmony of the group and lose your own impulse: Where do I want to go? What do I want? These questions remain in the background because the group provides orientation. Awareness: What do you want – yourself, all by yourself, without regard to the group? Is there a wish of your own that has been waiting for a long time? Exercise: Write down today: If I could decide on my own without disappointing anyone, what would I do next? Then think about whether you can take the first step.

Situation "Exhaustion & burnout" for subtype SX9. Autopilot: Stagnation sets in when you lose your boundaries with the other person: you passively drift along in your partner's rhythm, completely lacking your own direction. Your internal emptiness remains vague and unnamed. Awareness: What do you actually want—completely independent of the other person? Is there a personal direction inside you that you haven't tuned into for a long time? Exercise: Write down three sentences today that begin with: "I want..." Do this entirely for yourself, without factoring the other person into the equation at all. Let them stand. That is your direction.

Situation "Conflict & dispute" for subtype SX9. Autopilot: In conflict, you either merge with the other person's energy - accept their anger, carry it with you - or retreat into a silence that is difficult to achieve. Both are a form of being lost. Awareness: What are you – yourself – thinking and feeling in this conflict? Not the other, not the other's energy: you. Exercise: Say quietly what you want in this conflict - even if it contradicts the other person. Just for you, out loud: “I want…”

Situation "Loneliness & withdrawal" for subtype SX9. Autopilot: Loneliness is hardly recognized as such - you merge with your surroundings, your mood, your everyday life. Being alone runs in the background while you deal with the outside. It only appears in quiet moments. Awareness: When was the last time you really sought contact for yourself - not because it happened, not because someone else wanted it, but because you wanted it? Exercise: Initiate an encounter yourself today – don’t wait for someone to come. Choose active. Observe what it feels like when you approach someone out of yourself.

Situation "Decision making stress" for subtype SX9. Autopilot: You take on the decision of the most important person - merge with it, make it your own. Your own desire is so quiet that it can hardly be heard, and sometimes you no longer know what you actually wanted. Awareness: What decision are you really making here – your own, or one you inherited from someone else? Is there a difference? Exercise: Go outside for a moment alone, without your cell phone. Ask yourself: What would I choose in this matter if I were completely alone today? Write this down before you come back.

Situation "Relationship crisis" for subtype SX9. Autopilot: You merge with the other's mood, carry your crisis with you, lose yourself in the other's experience - and hardly notice what you need or think yourself. The relationship is in crisis and you are there but not fully there. Awareness: What do you need in this relationship crisis - yourself, separated from the other person? Is there something inside you that hasn't been heard yet? Exercise: Go outside alone for a moment. Ask yourself: What do I want for us - just for myself, without involving the other person? Then come back and share it.

Situation "Self-doubt & inner criticism" for subtype SX9. Autopilot: Self-doubt dissolves in the other: you adopt your partner's point of view - if he's okay, I'm okay. If he doubts, I doubt too. Your own assessment is missing because the boundaries are blurred. Awareness: What do you - yourself, independent of the other - think about yourself in this moment? Is there a separate voice that can judge this? Exercise: Write three sentences about yourself today that only come from you - without reference to the other person. “I am someone who…” Leave it as your own description.

Situation "Loss & grief" for subtype SX9. Autopilot: Loss of a central relationship brings deep disorientation: without the other person, you hardly know who you are. You look for support, snuggle up to what is familiar - and your own grief remains diffuse. Awareness: Who are you when you are alone with this loss - without the other person, without a purpose? What's there? Exercise: Go outside alone today, without a phone. Let the silence come. Ask yourself: What do I really feel - entirely for myself, without reference to anyone else?

Situation "Overwhelm & pressure" for subtype SX9. Autopilot: Overwhelm occurs when boundaries with the most important person or the environment are missing. You take on everything that comes – and lose track of your own capacity. Awareness: What of what you're wearing right now is really yours - and what did you take over because no one else was wearing it? Exercise: Make a list today: My tasks – and tasks that I have taken on. Then choose one from the second list and return it or leave it alone.

Situation "Stagnation & inner emptiness" for subtype SX9. Autopilot: Stagnation occurs when there are no boundaries with the other person: you move to your partner's rhythm without having your own direction. The inner emptiness remains diffuse and unnamed. Awareness: What do you want – regardless of the other person? Is there a direction within you that you haven't heard in a long time? Exercise: Today write three sentences that begin with “I want…” – just for you, without involving the other person. Leave them alone. This is your direction.
